title: The “official” map pin sells tickets
scenario: You search Maps for a popular attraction and tap a listing that looks official. The booking page shows today nearly sold out and asks for your passport number plus full card details to issue “named-entry tickets.”

answers.A: Navigate to the attraction’s official website from a trusted source and compare ticket requirements and availability there.
answers.B: Call the attraction or tourist office through contact details you verify independently before entering identity data.
answers.C: Book through the map listing if reviews are numerous and recent, since fake listings rarely build that history.

explanation: Search and map listings can be manipulated. High review counts do not justify unnecessary identity collection.
proTip: A map pin is a discovery tool, not proof of ownership.
